test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements regarding the Industrial Sector in India post the launch of the New Economic Policy in 1991 is/are NOT correct?

1. Compulsory licensing on several industries was abolished.

2. Many industries that were only reserved for the government were dereserved.

3. There was quota and price control for all the goods produced in the industrial sector.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The New Economic Policy of 1991 aimed at liberalization, privatization, and globalization, drastically altering India's industrial landscape.
 
• Compulsory licensing was abolished for most industries except for a few sectors like alcohol, hazardous chemicals, and pharmaceuticals.
 
• Several industries, previously reserved for the government, were dereserved, allowing private sector participation.
 
• The statement "There was quota and price control for all goods produced in the industrial sector" is incorrect as the policy eliminated most price controls and quotas to promote a free-market economy.
 
• Post-1991, industries experienced reduced government intervention, which led to increased competition and efficiency in production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liberalization:**

 
 
• The 1991 reforms reduced trade barriers, eased restrictions on foreign investments, and promoted economic openness.
 
• Licensing requirements were removed for most industries, except for a few critical sectors.
 
 
 
• **Privatization:**
 
 
• Many public sector enterprises were privatized or opened up for private participation.
 
• This led to an increase in efficiency and better resource allocation in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Globalization:**
 
 
• Foreign companies were allowed to invest in Indian markets, which boosted technology transfer and competition.
 
• The reforms integrated India's economy with the global markets, leading to export growth.
 
 
 
• **Price Controls:**
 
 
• Price controls and quotas were largely abolished, promoting a free-market economy.
 
• This allowed industries to determine prices based on market demand and supply rather than government mandates.
